column9: An electron dot diagram for magnesium shows…
column28: Magnesium is in group 2, so it has 2 valence electrons. A dot diagram shows only valence electrons: 2 dots.

column4: Why atoms bond and electron dot structures
column9: In an electron dot diagram, what is the most dots you draw on any one side of the symbol?
column28: Each side holds at most one pair: 4 sides × 2 = 8 dots in all.

column4: Why atoms bond and electron dot structures
column9: Which pair would form an IONIC bond?
column28: Ionic bonds form between a metal (sodium) and a nonmetal (chlorine). Sodium gives its electron to chlorine.

column9: The electron dot diagram of a main-group element X is shown. Which group is X in?
column28: Count the dots: 2 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 5 valence electrons. Main-group elements with 5 valence electrons are in group 15.

column4: Why atoms bond and electron dot structures
column9: How many valence electrons — and dots — does boron have?
column28: Boron is in group 13, so it has 3 valence electrons and 3 dots.

column4: Why atoms bond and electron dot structures
column9: Use the shaded element's place on the periodic table. What is its usual oxidation number (ion charge)? Include the sign (+ or −). Charge: ___
column28: The shaded element is sulfur, group 16, with 6 valence electrons. It gains 2 electrons to fill its outer level, so its charge is −2.

column4: Why atoms bond and electron dot structures
column9: In an ionic bond, how many potassium atoms does one oxygen atom need so that every atom ends up with a full outer level?
column28: Each potassium gives away 1 electron. Oxygen has 6 valence electrons and needs 2 more, so it takes 1 electron from each of 2 potassium atoms (K₂O).

column4: Why atoms bond and electron dot structures
column9: Why don't noble gases form compounds?
column15: They already have 8 valence electrons (helium has 2), so they are stable
column28: Noble gases already have a full outer level, so they have no reason to gain, lose, or share electrons.

column4: Why atoms bond and electron dot structures
column9: Which particles are involved in bonding?
column28: Only the outermost (valence) electrons are given, taken, or shared in a bond.

column4: Why atoms bond and electron dot structures
column9: Element X is in period 4. Its electron dot diagram is shown. Which element is X, and what ion does it form?
column28: One dot means group 1; period 4, group 1 is potassium. It loses its 1 valence electron, forming K⁺.

column4: Why atoms bond and electron dot structures
column28: Potassium (group 1) loses its single valence electron, giving it a +1 charge: K⁺.
